subject: Throughput crunch impacting LedgerOne - rapid response & exec coordination
messages:
From: Andi Russo <andi@ledgerone.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: LedgerOne SRE Team <sre@ledgerone.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:42:12 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden error/latency spike - production - urgent

Hi Rachel,

We've been seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and P95 latency for our production routes since ~08:30 PDT. Errors are concentrated on text-gen endpoints backed by our reserved capacity pool. Last 30m: 18% 5xx rate, P95 ~1.9s (previously 650ms). Our dashboard attached (screenshot) shows queue growth and token wait times.

This is directly impacting checkout personalization (customer-visible). Can Redwood confirm whether the dedicated GPU pool for our reservation is saturated or if there's an upstream throttling/fallback happening? We need:
- current utilization and active job count for our pool
- whether any noisy neighbors or cross-tenant spillover is present
- immediate mitigations to reduce 5xx and lower P95

PagerDuty: PD-98321. SLA window still open. Please escalate as needed.

Thanks,
Andi Russo
Head of Engineering (LedgerOne)

1) David (infra) will triage hot path, confirm whether GPU slot exhaustion or scheduler imbalance.

—Rachel

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: sudden error/latency spike - production - urgent

On Thu, Jun 3, 2027 at 09:42 AM Andi Russo <andi@ledgerone.com> wrote:
> We've been seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and P95 latency for our production routes since ~08:30 PDT.

Quick triage update from infra:
- Observed: the reserved GPU pool tied to LedgerOne (reservation id hb-4872) hit sustained 98% active slot utilization around 08:25. There is a correlated rise in per-request queue depth and backpressure on our continuous-batching scheduler.
- No evidence of cross-tenant noisy neighbor CPU/GPU stealing; the backlog is within the reserved shard.
- Root cause hypothesis: a sudden traffic delta for a heavy-generation path combined with an evicted KV-cache warmup leading to longer per-token latencies; this cascaded into queue overflow on a small subset of workers, generating 5xx when the token buffer was exhausted.

Mitigations we've applied (now):
- Enabled transient burst capacity (30m window): routed 12% of traffic to adjacent dedicated pool capacity to relieve the immediate queue.
- Dropped batching window slightly for that reservation's high-latency route to process more requests at lower per-batch latency (trade CPU utilization).
- Activated model fallback for non-critical endpoints: requests that can tolerate slightly shorter generations now go to gpt-small-1-quant (validated compatibility).

Next actions (ETA):
- 11:30: monitor P95 and 5xx in 15m windows; if improvement < 60% we will extend burst and recommend a temporary quota bump.
- By EOD: produce a short incident note with timeline and recommended permanent remediation (KV cache pinning, adjusted autoscale thresholds, and longer burst allotment in contract).

Attachments: short monitoring clip and sample slow stack trace (pushed to the shared drive).

David
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Andi Russo <andi@ledgerone.com>, Procurement <procure@ledgerone.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 16:12:02 -07:00
Subject: Post-triage summary & exec ask — LedgerOne throughput crunch

Andi / LedgerOne procurement —

Summary (current state):
- Immediate mitigations reduced the 5xx rate from ~18% to ~4.5% and P95 dropped from ~1.9s to ~720ms after enabling a 30-minute burst and model-fallback on non-critical routes.
- Backlog is trending down but we are still above normal headroom for the reservation during peak windows.

Requesting executive coordination:
- Authorization for a temporary quota increase (30% for 72 hours) or extended burst windows while we finalize a longer-term capacity plan (technical fixes + contractual change). This will avoid rolling customer-facing degradations overnight.
- If procurement approves, we'll formalize a short amendment (MOU) to cover burst billing and update the MAP. Attached is a draft mutual action plan for your review.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Procurement sign-off on 72-hour quota bump OR approval to continue rolling bursts while we implement KV-cache pinning.
2) Engineering (David) to deliver a remediation RFC by EOD tomorrow: autoscale threshold adjustments, pre-warming KV on failover, and per-route batching tuning.
3) CS (Neha) to open a formal support case note and propose a goodwill credit for the affected usage window.

If you want me to pull in a Senior Exec (Marissa) for an authorization call, I can schedule a 30-min bridge now — will coordinate once I hear from procurement.

Thanks — we will continue to monitor and post hourly updates.

—Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
